# Container borders (Subtle vs Pale)

**Figma:** Color/Border/Neutral — Subtle (actionable) · Pale (non-actionable)  
**Import:** `/* tokens */ var(--zen-color-border-neutral-subtle-default) · var(--zen-color-border-neutral-pale-default)`

Pick the border of a closed container (a stroke or ring enclosing a box on all sides) by whether the box can be acted on: Subtle for actionable, Pale for non-actionable. Dashed strokes are always at least Subtle.

## Use it for
- Subtle: closed boxes the user clicks, taps, focuses, types into, drags or selects — buttons, chips, tags, segmented items, checkbox/radio marks, every form field (Read-only included), clickable cards and rows, drop zones.
- Pale: closed boxes that only group or frame content — static cards, panels, surfaces, callout frames, preview wells, non-clickable logo or info tiles.
- Subtle for every dashed line or stroke — dashed dividers, dashed empty states and drop zones, the Read-only field's dash — even on a static box (a dash has less ink, so Pale is too faint).

## Use something else for
- Solid lines and single edges — toolbar separators, row rules, the Tab baseline, the Sidebar tree-line, a section border-top, the Accordion Divider rule: not covered by the container rule, follow Figma (Subtle or Pale). A Divider defaults to Pale; Medium (Subtle) and High (Solid) only when the design calls for more.
- Strokes around media — avatars, photos, visuals, illustrations, graphics, thumbnails: not covered (Subtle allowed).
- Component border tokens (Button-Tertiary, Chip-Secondary, Tag, Checkbox, Radio-Button, Segmented-Item) — use them instead of raw Neutral tokens.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actionable box | `--zen-color-border-neutral-subtle-*` | default · hover · pressed; selected → Color/Border/Active/*; disabled → Color/Border/Disabled |
| Non-actionable box | `--zen-color-border-neutral-pale-default` | no interaction states |
| Dashed line/stroke | `--zen-color-border-neutral-subtle-default` | overrides static → Pale |
| Divider | `Default · Medium · High` | Pale (default) · Subtle · Solid |

## ✅ Do
- Decide in four questions: is it dashed? → Subtle. Is it a solid line, a single edge or a media stroke? → not covered (a divider defaults to Pale). Does the box itself handle click/change/focus/drag or is it a form control? → Subtle. Otherwise → Pale.
- Keep a static box Pale even when it holds actionable children; the children bring their own Subtle borders.
- Give actionable borders their hover/pressed steps (…-subtle-hover / -pressed).

## ❌ Don't
- Don't frame a static box with Subtle — it falsely signals interactivity.
- Don't frame a box the user can act on with Pale — it reads as disabled or static.
- Don't give a Pale container border hover or pressed feedback.
- Don't draw a dashed line or stroke with Pale or a raw colour.
- Don't pick the token by how strong you want the line to look.
- Don't hard-code a border colour in component CSS; use tokens (harness: color/token-only).

## Accessibility
- A border is never the only cue for interactivity; pair it with cursor, focus ring and a role.

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `border/subtle-static-box` | warn | A closed box nobody can act on is framed with Neutral/Pale; Neutral/Subtle signals an actionable container. | `zen-allow-subtle-static-box: <reason>` |
| `border/pale-actionable-box` | warn | Actionable containers (hover/press/focus, form controls, clickable cards) use Neutral/Subtle; Pale has no interaction states. | `zen-allow-pale-actionable-box: <reason>` |
| `border/dashed-is-subtle` | warn | Dashed lines and strokes (dashed dividers, empty states, drop zones, Read-only fields) use Neutral/Subtle — never Pale or a raw colour. | `zen-allow-dashed-color: <reason>` |
| `color/token-only` | error | Component CSS uses --zen-* colour tokens (raw values only as var() fallbacks); raw colours break theme and mode switching. | `zen-allow-raw-colour: <reason>` |
